reason: The goal is to supply the muscle fibers, and sugar is described as their fuel.
expectation: The sugar will supply fuel to the muscle fibers; oxygen may also be needed.

effect: Sugar is broken into smaller fuel pieces in the cell fluid, producing some ATP; oxygen still appears needed for the supply goal.
reaction: The picture makes the first stage of fuel processing clear.
reason: The goal calls for oxygen as well as fuel, and the processed fuel pieces move toward a mitochondrion.
expectation: Oxygen will help the muscle fibers use the processed fuel to support continued cellular work.

effect: Oxygen completed the supply goal, and the ATP cycle shows how fuel energy supports repeated muscle work. The next goal is to collect and transmit the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The cycle helps connect the fuel supply to muscle work.
reason: The connective wrapping is pictured fitting around a group of muscle cells, so it should help collect their pulls.
expectation: The wrapping will bundle the muscle fibers into a structure that can collect their pulls.

effect: The wrapping gathers the fibers into muscle bundles, with their pulls directed toward the ends; tendons are still needed.
reaction: The arrows make the purpose of the wrapping clear.
reason: The tendon cords should transmit the bundled pulls, and the front tendons are available.
expectation: The front tendons will attach to the muscle bundles to help transmit their pull.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons also appear suited to transmitting a pull.

effect: The front tendons produced bending muscles; the tendon needs an attachment to move a joint. Rear tendons remain available for the second muscle group.
reaction: The result makes the tendon's role clear, though the joint is still absent.
reason: The rear tendons appear to be the remaining parts needed to form the second muscle group.
expectation: The rear tendons will attach to muscle bundles to create the other muscle group.

effect: The rear tendons formed straightening muscles and completed the goal; both muscle groups now have tendons, though bones are still absent.
reaction: The paired muscle groups make the outcome clear, but I am curious how they will move a joint.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the connective wrapping was most worthwhile: the picture connects individual cell pulls to a larger pull through the shared wrapping.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the second set of tendons felt predictable after the first, though it completed the pair of muscle groups.

surprise.text: The ATP cycle changed my understanding by showing that muscle work uses ATP while cells keep remaking it using fuel energy.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the two muscle groups attach to bones and move a joint, since the tendons are present but the bones are still absent.
